extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, processors, importers, exporters, and compliance officers for chemical substances subject to EPA SNURs; regulatory/legal professionals advising such entities
extracted.subtask_short: TSCA SNUR compliance for listed chemicals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for complying with EPA Significant New Use Rules (SNURs) for a set of specified chemical substances, including notification, submission, recordkeeping, and use-specific restrictions. Covers procedures for submitting Significant New Use Notices (SNUNs), confidentiality (CBI) procedures, testing/monitoring guidance, and specified prohibited or restricted uses for each listed substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90-day pre-notification requirement for significant new uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons must notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any listed chemical substance for an activity that is designated as a 'significant new use' in the SNUR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the use within the applicable review period. Persons may not commence manufacture or processing for the significant new use until they have submitted a Significant New Use Notice (SNUN), EPA has conducted a review of the notice, made an appropriate determination on the notice, and has taken any required risk management actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'manufacture' includes import
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the SNURs, 'manufacture' is defined by statute to include import.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities that import the chemical substances in bulk form, as part of a mixture, or as part of an article (if required by rule) must treat importing as manufacture and comply with SNUR notification and certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNUN submission format and procedure (EPA Form 7710-25 / e-PMN)
rubrics_metrics.description: SNUNs must be submitted on EPA Form No. 7710-25, generated using e-PMN software, and submitted in accordance with procedures in 40 CFR 720.40 and 721.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-PMN software is available electronically at EPA's new chemicals website. Submission includes registration for EPA's Central Data Exchange (CDX) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to include in SNUNs (possession/control and reasonably ascertainable)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of an applicable TSCA section 4 rule/order, persons are required to submit only information in their possession or control and to describe any other information known to or reasonably ascertainable by them (see 40 CFR 720.50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rule, order, or consent agreement under TSCA section 4 requires submission of information for the chemical substance, that information must be submitted with the SNUN. Submitters are encouraged to provide potentially useful information identified in the proposed rule's Unit IV to assist EPA's analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA authority to require testing and encouragement to consult on test protocols and NAMs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has authority to require appropriate testing upon review of PMNs and SNUNs; TSCA does not otherwise require development of particular new information prior to SNUN submission except as noted under section 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA strongly encourages submitters to consult with the Agency before performing any testing to help select protocols. Under TSCA section 4(h), EPA encourages consultation on alternative test methods and strategies (New Approach Methodologies, NAMs) to reduce vertebrate animal testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: CBI procedure for significant new uses (40 CFR 721.11) and bona fide intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain significant new uses may be claimed as Confidential Business Information (CBI). Under 40 CFR 721.11, a manufacturer or processor may request EPA identify the confidential significant new use by showing bona fide intent to manufacture or process the chemical substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If EPA concludes bona fide intent has been shown, EPA will identify the confidential significant new use to that person. When chemical identities are also CBI, manufacturers/processors can combine the bona fide submission into a single step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated cutoff date for determining ongoing uses
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA designates December 6, 2019, as the cutoff date for determining whether the new use is ongoing for the chemical substances covered by these SNURs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA generally designates a use as significant as of the date of publication of the proposed rule (to prevent initiating a new use during the pendency of the rule). Uses ongoing as of the proposed rule publication that did not cease before issuance of the final rule will not be designated as significant new uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements (§721.125) applicable to manufacturers/processors
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers and processors of the listed substances must comply with recordkeeping requirements specified in §721.125 (applicable subsections listed in each chemical-specific section, e.g., (a) through (c) and (i) or (k)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chemical section specifies which subsections of §721.125 apply. Recordkeeping applies to manufacturers and processors of the substance and is part of Subpart A provisions unless modified in the chemical-specific section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation or revocation of certain notification requirements (§721.185)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of §721.185 (limitation or revocation of certain notification requirements) apply to the sections for the listed chemical substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §721.185 for circumstances under which notification requirements may be limited or revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workplace protection measures for P-17-299 (§721.63)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the chemical identified as PMN P-17-299, the significant new use 'Protection in the workplace' invokes requirements specified in §721.63(a)(4) through (6) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining which persons are reasonably likely to be exposed (§721.63(4)), engineering controls (e.g., enclosure or confinement, general and local ventilation) or administrative controls (e.g., workplace policies and procedures) must be considered and implemented where feasible. For purposes of §721.63(a)(5), respirators must provide a NIOSH assigned protection factor (APF) of at least 1,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial, commercial, and consumer activity limits for specific substances (§721.80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several listed substances designate certain industrial, commercial, and consumer activities as significant new uses, invoking requirements specified in §721.80 (with subsection pointers per chemical). Examples include: using a substance other than as a thickener in paint; using a substance in concentrations greater than 1% in formulated products; use other than as a clear coat for wood; use other than as an auxiliary drier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chemical-specific section spells out the particular §721.80 subparagraph (e.g., §721.80(f) or §721.80(o)) and the specific activities (including concentration thresholds and functional uses) that are designated as significant new uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of consumer-product exceptions and restrictions (example: architectural coatings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For PMN P-18-172, it is a significant new use to use the substance in a consumer product except for use in architectural coatings; EPA removed designation for consumer architectural coatings based on comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comments identifying ongoing uses can lead to modification of the final rule to exclude certain ongoing uses from the SNUR's significant new use designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition/limitation on inhalation-exposure uses (PMN P-19-118)
rubrics_metrics.description: For PMN P-19-118 (generic substituted polyalkylenepoly reaction products), it is a significant new use to manufacture, process, or use the substance in any manner that results in inhalation exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such uses are subject to the SNUN requirement and invoked Subpart A/§721 provisions as modified in the chemical-specific section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release-to-water significant new use and §721.90 requirements (N values)
rubrics_metrics.description: For certain listed substances (e.g., §721.11420 and §721.11446), 'Release to water' is designated a significant new use and invokes requirements specified in §721.90(a)(4), (b)(4), and (c)(4) where an N value (e.g., N=22 or N=78) is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult §721.90 for the specific release-to-water reporting, testing, and limitation requirements associated with the referenced N value and subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export notification requirements (TSCA section 12(b) / 40 CFR part 707 subpart D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who export or intend to export a chemical substance identified in the SNUR are subject to the export notification provisions of TSCA section 12(b) and must comply with the export notification requirements in 40 CFR part 707, subpart D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A one-time notice to EPA must be provided for the first export or intended export to a particular country. Costs per notification vary by chemical and number of countries; the economic analysis estimates approximately $106 per unit notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import certification requirements (TSCA section 13 and 19 CFR cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical importers are subject to TSCA section 13 and the implementing import provisions (19 CFR 12.118 through 12.127) and must certify that shipments comply with all applicable rules and Orders under TSCA (including §§5,6,7 and Title IV regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA policy in support of import certification is at 40 CFR part 707, subpart B. Importers should ensure proper certifications accompany shipments and evaluate whether the SNUR applies to imported forms (bulk, mixtures, articles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic burden, fees, and estimated time burden for SNUN submission
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's estimates: preparing and submitting a SNUN is approximately $45,000 per submission for large businesses and $14,500 for qualifying small businesses (includes CDX registration and user fee). The SNUN user fee is typically $37,000 or a reduced $6,480 for qualifying small businesses (per 40 CFR 700.45(c)). The estimated annual burden is between 30 and 170 hours per submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are estimates and reflect fees as known at the time of rulemaking; no company incurs these costs unless it decides to pursue the significant new use. EPA offers reduced fees for qualifying small businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to provide exposure and release information in SNUNs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA indicates it will be better able to evaluate SNUNs that provide detailed information on human exposure and environmental release that may result from the significant new use of the chemical substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not mandatory (except where TSCA section 4 requires testing), providing detailed exposure/release information may reduce the likelihood EPA takes immediate regulatory actions under TSCA sections 5(e) or 5(f). Submitters are encouraged to contact EPA early enough to conduct appropriate tests when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart A applicability with section-specific modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of Subpart A of Part 721 apply to each chemical-specific section except as modified by the paragraph (b) of that section (which lists applicable recordkeeping and other modifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the specific chemical section for any deviations from Subpart A; many sections explicitly list which subsections of §721.125 apply and reference §721.185 for limitation/revocation of notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of public comments and potential modification of SNURs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA considered public comments on the proposed rule; comments identifying ongoing uses resulted in modified final rules for particular chemical substances (e.g., removing certain uses from significant new use designation). A Response to Public Comments document is available in the docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may submit comments during notice-and-comment periods; comments that identify documented ongoing uses can change the final SNUR designations. Consult the docket for comment summaries and EPA responses.
